subject: Planned model compatibility sunset — readiness ladder & comms asks
messages:
From: Liz Morales <liz@datagrid.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Upcoming model change — quick ask on runway and exceptions

Hi Irene,

Quick background: DataGrid relies on your embeddings endpoint for search ranking in two tiers of traffic (primary + fallback). We just saw the note about the plan to promote inference-v2 models into the default catalog in August. Before that goes live we need to understand the compatibility characteristics and what migration runway Redwood is planning.

Two asks from our side:
- Can you confirm whether inference-v2 changes embed dimensionality or tokenization behavior (we've seen occasional drift in internal experiments)?
- If you proceed with the default switch, what is the official deprecation notice window and what exception process exists if a customer needs an extended runway?

Attached two small artifacts: data_grid_usage_report_Q2.csv (sample of request sizes) and sample-api-usage.log (anonymized). Those should help estimate impact.

We'd like to propose a mutual action plan (MAP) so our engineering and CS teams can schedule the migration. Can we get the proposed timeline + recommended migration steps by next week?

Thanks — appreciate the help.

— Liz
Product Manager, DataGrid

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Morales <liz@datagrid.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming model change — quick ask on runway and exceptions

Hi Liz — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts, helpful. Looping in Sales (Ben), Comms (Lauren), Product (Marcus) and CS (Monica) so we can coordinate an operational plan.

Initial answers and internal asks:
- Dimensionality/tokenization: short answer — no dimensionality change planned for the standard embeddings configuration in inference-v2, but quantization and updated pre/post processing may produce small drift for certain prompts (Marcus will expand).
- Deprecation window: our proposed default is a 60-day public notice followed by a 90-day migration window before we start routing non-pinned traffic to v2. We can support a temporary compatibility bridge for high-risk customers for an additional 12 weeks under an exception.

Internal asks:
- Ben: confirm commercial concessions for customers who require extra runway (credits / invoice offsets).
- Lauren: draft a short customer-facing comms + migration checklist.
- Marcus: propose a canary plan (routing/alias + fallback policy + recommended batch configs).
- Monica: prepare CS playbook and capture a list of customers who should get proactive outreach.

I'll draft a proposed MAP and share with the group by Monday. Liz — can you confirm whether your migration will need the compatibility bridge or if you plan to pin a legacy model during your migration? That will determine the commercial asks.

Best,
Irene
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming model change — quick ask on runway and exceptions

Thanks Irene — quick commercial note: we should offer a standard exception package (up to 12 weeks) with a predefined credit schedule to avoid case-by-case negotiations. It keeps renewals simple and reduces lift on AE/finance.

I attached a short template we use for exception approvals: contract-exception-template.docx — legal can fast-track this if we follow the exact fields. For very large customers (>$250k ARR) we should consider a short-term SLA addendum rather than credits.

I'll coordinate with procurement@acme.com and similar contacts if DataGrid confirms they need the bridge.

- Ben
VP Sales

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming model change — quick ask on runway and exceptions

Great thread — technical context and recommended plan below.

TL;DR: v2 has a more aggressive quantization fallback for GPU memory savings which can change embedding vectors’ L2 norms for certain prompt shapes. No tokenization or dimensionality changes.

Recommended steps:
1) Canary (2% production traffic) for 2 weeks with continuous embedding drift monitoring (we'll surface cosine similarity deltas).
2) Alias routing: create model alias "embed-stable" that points to inference-v1 by default; switch alias to v2 for a subset once canary passes. This avoids breaking pinned calls.
3) Compatibility bridge: a short-lived shim that reroutes requests with the "compat=true" header to v1 for customers under exception. Requires a small routing config and a flag in the console — low infra work but needs product signoff.
4) Batch tuning: recommend conservative max_batch_tokens for v2 initially (we'll provide suggested settings in the playbook).

Attachments: compatibility-bridge-proposal.pdf (detailed infra change) and migration-map.xlsx (timeline & rollout gates).

I'll also add a short evaluation script and a Kibana dashboard (INF-832) for teams to check drift and latency regressions. Marcus
PM, Serving Runtime

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Morales <liz@datagrid.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming model change — readiness ladder & comms asks

Liz — thanks for starting the conversation and for the sample artifacts. Summary / proposed MAP below (please reply with confirmations or edits):

Proposed MAP (high level):
- Week 0 (today): internal alignment and MAP signoff (this email thread).
- Week 1: public customer notice draft and targeted outreach to top 25 risk customers. Lauren to own comms.
- Weeks 2–3: canary run (2% traffic). Marcus to publish drift dashboard and recommended batch configs.
- Weeks 4–6: open migration window; customers can pin inference-v1 or request a compatibility bridge under exception. Ben will surface exception pricing.
- Weeks 7–12: extended-bridge window for approved exceptions (12-week stopgap).

Asks for DataGrid: please confirm by EOD Friday whether you need the compatibility bridge or if you will pin v1 during migration. If you opt for the bridge, indicate the expected RPS and a sample traffic snapshot (we can use the CSV you already sent).

Deliverables we will provide: internal playbook link (see below), a migration checklist for your engineers, a drift monitoring dashboard, and a pre-authorized exception doc for faster approvals.

Links / attachments: compatibility-bridge-proposal.pdf, migration-map.xlsx, and our internal playbook: https://drive.redwood.company/drive/folders/compatibility-playbook. I've also linked the HubSpot record for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890.

If you want a short 30-minute sync to finalize the MAP, Ben and Marcus are available on Thursday 5–6pm PT; otherwise we'll proceed with the cadence above and circulate the comms draft tomorrow.

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmation.

— Irene
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
